transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-22 14:30 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (BlueMap - Head of ML), Tom Ellis (BlueMap - Infra Lead), Sara Nguyen (BlueMap - Security)

Summary: high-level discovery to understand current OpenAI/Anthropic + vLLM/TGI stack, compatibility concerns for on-prem routing, and pilot scope for eval parity. Customer wary of data residency, KMS, and latency for last-mile logistics inference.

Topics: 1) current stack & pain points; 2) vLLM/TGI parity questions; 3) hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private); 4) security + compliance; 5) next steps / bench plan.

00:00:03 Maya Chen: hey everyone, uh thanks for taking the time. quick intro, i'm maya from redwood, i'm the account lead, with diego, our se.
00:00:10 Priya Raman: hey thanks, yep i'm priya, head of ml at bluemap. we've been working on a mixture of openai stuff and some self-hosted vllm for cost reasons.
00:00:20 Tom Ellis: tom here, infra lead, i run the k8s clusters where vLLM lives and also aws stuff.
00:00:27 Sara Nguyen: sara from security, i'll mostly ask compliance questions.
00:00:33 Diego Alvarez: great, quick agenda — we want to understand your latency/cost targets, current throughput, model families, and any must-have security constraints.
00:00:45 Priya Raman: sure. high level — we have a user-facing routing for last-mile delivery ETA & document summarization feature. latency target is p95 sub-500ms for short prompts (<128 tokens), and we run heavy batch jobs overnight. cost is a big driver; openai is too expensive at scale.
00:01:05 Maya Chen: makes sense — when you say openai are you on chat completions or embeddings primarily?
00:01:11 Priya Raman: mostly chat/completions with GPT-4o variants for quality, and embeddings via openai for semantic search. We've been moving embeddings to a managed vector store but still using openai for quality.
00:01:25 Tom Ellis: and on-prem we run vLLM with TGI wrappers for some models — mostly llama-family and a couple of mosaic/alliances models, apologies, mosaic ml, the names get messy.
00:01:38 Diego Alvarez: understood. two quick clarifying items: 1) are you using kv cache persistence between requests? 2) what's your typical sequence length distribution?
00:01:46 Priya Raman: we persist kv cache for conversational sessions so we get re-use across multi-turn. sequence distribution is mostly 32-256 tokens for interactive, with some long-form at 1k tokens for batch generation.
00:01:58 Maya Chen: good — that shapes batching and cache handling for cost. question for sara on security: any hard constraints on customer-managed keys / HSM?
00:02:07 Sara Nguyen: yes, we need KMS integration and prefer BYOK for pilot if possible. also SOC2 type 2 is table stakes, and we have an internal audit that wants immutable audit logs for admin actions.
00:02:20 Maya Chen: redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and detailed audit logging; diego can share the integration doc after this call.
00:02:28 Diego Alvarez: yeah, i'll attach the kms runbook.
00:02:31 Priya Raman: great. can you also comment on model parity — we've tuned models with vLLM and TGI, and we worry about outputs differing when we move to hosted or dedicated.
00:02:41 Diego Alvarez: absolutely. parity has two parts: 1) model byte-to-byte parity — which depends on tokenizer, precision (fp16 vs int8), and kernel implementations; 2) infra-level behavior — attention, kv cache handling, and sampling RNG. we aim to produce the same top-level outputs, but exact tokens may vary between runtimes like vLLM vs our runtime, especially if quantized.
00:03:02 Tom Ellis: so if we run TGI locally and benchmark against redwood hosted, are you able to run a parity bench that uses our prompt set and reports latency/cost/quality deltas?
00:03:12 Diego Alvarez: yes — typical plan: we run the same prompt suite through your local vLLM/TGI and through our hosted/dedicated variants with identical model weights where possible. we'll normalize tokenization and sampling seeds when supported. caveat: some open-source kernels and quantization flags can change outputs.
00:03:28 Priya Raman: okay — what about quantization? we're using 4-bit quantization for cost saving in vLLM; will that make parity impossible?
00:03:36 Diego Alvarez: quantization will change exact outputs, but we can compare at the quality metric level (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-similarity/LLM-eval metrics). We'll run both int8/int4 variants in a controlled way. If you need bitwise matching, that's typically only possible with the same runtime and artifacts.
00:03:54 Sara Nguyen: on the private side — we might need an air-gapped option for certain customers. do you offer a private deployment that can be installed on-prem?
00:04:03 Maya Chen: yes — redwood private is available; we provide a customer-managed control plane and on-prem runtime artifacts. there's an enterprise onboarding flow. Diego: we can sketch the install footprint now.
00:04:13 Diego Alvarez: footprint wise: for the LLM runtime with M60-equivalent nodes — sorry, i meant A100 or H100-like — you're looking at N GPUs depending on model size. For our Dedicated offering we can reserve pools in the same region to meet your latency. For Private, we ship an installer but you manage networking.
00:04:32 Tom Ellis: can the private deployment integrate with our existing k8s + Istio mesh? we prefer not to add another overlay network.
00:04:40 Diego Alvarez: yes, we've done k8s operators and a containerized runtime that works with existing meshes; some teams prefer a managed node pool to reduce ops burden.
00:04:51 Priya Raman: how do you handle fallbacks — say high traffic spikes? we want graceful degradation rather than errors.
00:04:58 Maya Chen: smart routing supports policy-based fallback — route to cheaper model variants or a different region; we also support burst capacity for Dedicated customers.
00:05:08 Tom Ellis: latency question — you mentioned p95 under 500ms. is that realistic for H100-backed dedicated? what about network egress from aws region?
00:05:17 Diego Alvarez: for short prompts on H100-backed Dedicated in-region, sub-500ms p95 is realistic; for hosted multi-tenant there can be slightly higher tail latencies depending on burst load. We can run a latency bench as part of the pilot.
00:05:29 Priya Raman: another constraint: we need audit trails for prompt provenance and redaction for pii. do you capture prompts in logs by default?
00:05:37 Maya Chen: by default we capture metadata and token counts; we can redact prompts or send them to customer-managed storage via KMS. We also have token-level cost reporting.
00:05:46 Sara Nguyen: good. any SOC 2 evidence we can review quickly?
00:05:50 Maya Chen: yes, i'll send the SOC 2 report and our security pack after the call.
00:05:55 Priya Raman: on the migration path — ideally we want minimal code changes. our current infra calls an internal adapter that proxies to openai or local tgi. can we keep that adapter and just swap endpoints?
00:06:05 Diego Alvarez: yes — the Redwood API is drop-in REST gRPC compatible and SDKs are similar. we maintain model catalog names and a routing layer so you can route by model alias. Some customers add a small shim for secret rotation/KMS.
00:06:17 Tom Ellis: what about cost modeling — we need to compare our current vLLM infra cost vs hosted/dedicated. do you help with that analysis?
00:06:25 Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Optimize can produce cost simulation considering batching, KV cache hit rates, and quantization. we'll need sample traffic and token distribution from you to model.
00:06:34 Priya Raman: we can share a week's worth of traces sanitized.
00:06:38 Diego Alvarez: perfect. for the parity bench, would you prefer us to run in your cloud account or run against hosted redwood endpoints?
00:06:46 Tom Ellis: probably both — run from our infra to account for egress and routing, and also a hosted-to-hosted run.
00:06:52 Diego Alvarez: ok, plan: we'll run three legs: 1) your vLLM/TGI from your infra; 2) Redwood Dedicated in-region; 3) Redwood Hosted. we'll measure latency, cost, and quality metrics.
00:07:04 Priya Raman: timeline — we want a pilot in ~2 weeks if possible.
00:07:08 Maya Chen: that aligns; Diego, can you own the bench plan and estimate infra we need?
00:07:12 Diego Alvarez: i'll draft it and share by monday, target run next week.
00:07:16 Priya Raman: needs to include our prompt set and the multi-turn sessions.
00:07:19 Diego Alvarez: yes, include kv cache persistence emulation.
00:07:22 Sara Nguyen: on contracts — we need data residency clauses and deletion guarantees after pilot. is that standard?
00:07:28 Maya Chen: yes, we can include data handling and deletion terms; for hosted there's an option for 30-day retention or custom retention policies for enterprise.
00:07:36 Tom Ellis: question about model weights — can we bring our own models? we have a tuned Llama variant with proprietary finetune.
00:07:44 Diego Alvarez: BYOM (bring your own model) is supported for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we have a vetting process and endpoint-specific rules. We'll document the steps to upload weights and manage access.
00:07:55 Priya Raman: good. also curious about SDKs — we have a python microservice and some go services. does redwood have go/pyt SDKs?
00:08:02 Maya Chen: yes — python, node, and go SDKs. the API mirrors standard patterns.
00:08:06 Priya Raman: ok. switching gears — can you explain debug/tracing — sometimes debugging prompts is tough in multitenant infra.
00:08:12 Diego Alvarez: we provide per-request trace IDs, token-level latency breakdowns, and per-route dashboards. For Dedicated/Private you can increase retention and add tracing hooks.
00:08:21 Priya Raman: great.
00:08:25 Tom Ellis: any limits on throughput? we need ~200 concurrent small requests during peak.
00:08:31 Diego Alvarez: for Dedicated we can reserve capacity to meet that concurrency; autoscaling plus burst policies can absorb spikes. we'll size pools based on bench results.
00:08:39 Maya Chen: i want to call out one risk: if you need exact byte-for-byte parity with your current vLLM int4 quantized runtime, that may not be achievable with hosted quantized kernels. our recommendation is to focus on eval parity via metrics and user-facing behavior.
00:08:55 Priya Raman: that's what i suspected. ok.
00:08:58 Sara Nguyen: compliance follow-ups — we'll expect a SOC 2 attestation, penetration test report, and a data processing addendum.
00:09:06 Maya Chen: we'll include those in the security pack.
00:09:10 Priya Raman: question — do you have customers in logistics or enterprise with similar latency needs?
00:09:15 Maya Chen: yes, we've worked with a few rideshare and delivery platforms; i'll redact case studies and share them.
00:09:22 Diego Alvarez: and we can share a sample benchmark showing sub-400ms p95 on Dedicated for <128 token prompts.
00:09:29 Tom Ellis: excellent.
00:09:33 Maya Chen: ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.
00:09:36 Maya Chen: recap: 1) Diego to draft parity bench (3 legs) and infra footprint; 2) Maya to send pricing + SOC2/security pack; 3) BlueMap to share sanitized traces and prompt set; 4) schedule pilot kickoff.
00:09:49 Priya Raman: agreed. timeline — maya, can you push pricing by tuesday?
00:09:53 Maya Chen: yes, i'll aim for 2027-04-26.
00:09:57 Diego Alvarez: i'll have the bench plan by 2027-04-29.
00:10:01 Sara Nguyen: we'll return the questionnaire by 2027-04-24.
00:10:05 Tom Ellis: i'll stand up a testing namespace to run vLLM/TGI tests.
00:10:09 Maya Chen: Perfect. Are there any other questions?
00:10:13 Priya Raman: one small thing — do you support per-route model aliasing so we can A/B?
00:10:18 Diego Alvarez: yes, canary and A/B rollouts are supported at routing layer.
00:10:22 Priya Raman: great.
00:10:24 Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with notes and links.
00:10:28 (crosstalk) Tom Ellis: thanks. bye.

[End of recorded transcript — subsequent conversation off-record about scheduling logistics.]
